dsprrr for DSPy users

Source: vignettes/dspy-comparison.Rmd
dspy-comparison.Rmd

dsprrr brings DSPy’s programming model to R on top of ellmer and tidyverse conventions. It keeps DSPy’s core concepts—signatures, modules, metrics, and teleprompters—without forcing Python idioms onto R: datasets are tibbles, signatures are immutable S7 values, modules are stateful R6 objects, and ellmer owns every provider call and structured schema. If you already know DSPy, this page maps what carries over, what differs, and what is still on the roadmap.

Side by side

A question-answering program, compiled with labeled few-shot examples and evaluated, in DSPy:

import dspy

dspy.configure(lm=dspy.LM("openai/gpt-6-luna"))

qa = dspy.Predict("question -> answer")
qa(question="What is the capital of France?").answer

def metric(example, pred, trace=None):
    return example.answer == pred.answer

trainset = [
    dspy.Example(question="What is 2 + 2?", answer="4").with_inputs("question"),
    # ...
]
devset = [
    dspy.Example(question="What is 3 + 5?", answer="8").with_inputs("question"),
    # ...
]
compiled = dspy.LabeledFewShot(k=3).compile(qa, trainset=trainset)
dspy.Evaluate(devset=devset, metric=metric)(compiled)

and in dsprrr:

library(dsprrr)

dsp_configure(provider = "openai", model = "gpt-6-luna")

qa <- module(signature("question -> answer"))
run(qa, question = "What is the capital of France?")$answer

metric <- function(prediction, expected) {
  prediction$answer == expected$answer
}

trainset <- data.frame(
  question = c("What is 2 + 2?", "Who wrote Hamlet?", "What is the largest planet?"),
  answer = c("4", "Shakespeare", "Jupiter")
)
devset <- data.frame(
  question = c("What is 3 + 5?", "Who painted the Mona Lisa?"),
  answer = c("8", "Leonardo da Vinci")
)
compiled <- qa |> compile(LabeledFewShot(k = 3L), trainset)
evaluate(compiled, devset, metric)

The examples below reuse qa, trainset, devset, and this default chat.

The everyday differences to keep in mind:

DSPy dsprrr
dspy.configure(lm=...) dsp_configure(), set_default_chat(), or .llm = per call
dspy.Predict("question -> answer") module(signature("question -> answer")); other constructors also take strings directly
pred.answer on a Prediction result$answer on a named list
metric(example, pred, trace=None) metric(prediction, expected): prediction first, expected is the whole data row
List of dspy.Example(...).with_inputs(...) A data frame; signature input names identify input columns
optimizer.compile(program, trainset=...) compile(program, optimizer, trainset) (returns a new program; original unchanged)
k=3 k = 3L: many S7 integer settings require an integer literal

Modules

DSPy dsprrr Notes
dspy.Predict module(sig) Core structured predictor
dspy.ChainOfThought chain_of_thought(), with_reasoning() Default "rationale" field, plus "plan" and "native" thinking modes
dspy.ReAct react(sig) Native ellmer tool turns, max_iterations, opt-in finalization = "submit"
dspy.ProgramOfThought (removed in DSPy 3.5) program_of_thought() Retained in dsprrr; generates and executes R code via runner or interpreter_factory
dspy.CodeAct (removed in DSPy 3.5) code_act() Retained in dsprrr; combines ellmer tools with R code execution
dspy.BestOfN best_of_n() Reward-guided retries
dspy.Refine refine() Retries with rendered feedback templates
dspy.MultiChainComparison multi_chain_comparison() Runs M CoT chains and reconciles them
dspy.RLM rlm_module() (experimental) Explores R objects iteratively with generate_action / extract predictors and SUBMIT()
dspy.Flex flex() (experimental) Bounded JSON predictor graphs or sandboxed R forward() programs optimized by GEPA
dspy.Parallel / Module.batch run_dataset(), .concurrency = concurrency_control(...) Batch execution via ellmer or mirai
dspy.majority ensemble() + reduce_majority() Plus reduce_weighted_vote() and reduce_best_by_metric()
dspy.KNN compile() with KNNFewShot() Bring your own vectorizer (e.g., ragnar::embed_openai())
Retrieval rag_module() + ragnar Plain R retrievers or ragnar stores (ragnar_tool())
Noul, Score, Choice (experimental) with_decisions() + decision_bool() / decision_score() / decision_choice() (experimental) Probability evidence via ellmer structured output, decoded locally; no “System One” classifier backend

Code-running modules (program_of_thought(), code_act(), rlm_module()) accept either a caller-owned runner or a per-call interpreter_factory. Executable flex() requires interpreter_factory and an enforced sandbox by default, while JSON flex() needs no interpreter; see Flex: optimize a whole program.

Reasoning modes, ReAct submit, history, and async

  • Reasoning modes: chain_of_thought() defaults to "rationale" (adds a reasoning field). Pass mode = "plan" for a concise plan field, or mode = "native" with .return_format = "structured" to keep the output schema unchanged and read provider thinking blocks from get_metadata(result)$native_reasoning.
  • ReAct finalization = "submit": Lets the model return its typed answer through a reserved submit tool call inside the tool loop (avoiding the extra structured-output request of the default finalization = "structured").
  • Portable conversation history: Scalar run() calls on react() and rlm_module() accept .history (from conversation_history(), get_history(), or load_history()) when .return_format = "structured", and persist safely as JSON with save_history(). ReAct preserves native turns without re-executing tools; RLM carries bounded textual summaries and requires an interpreter_factory. ReAct and RLM histories cannot be mixed, and dataset/async/streaming routes reject .history.
  • Async ReAct: run_async() awaits the full sequential ReAct tool loop and accepts .control = react_async_control(on_progress = ...) for ordered progress events and cooperative cancellation (control$cancel()). See Models, providers and streaming.
# Native reasoning + ReAct submit + portable history
native_qa <- chain_of_thought("question -> answer", mode = "native")
agent <- react("question -> answer", finalization = "submit")

first <- run(
  agent,
  question = "What is the capital of France?",
  .history = conversation_history(),
  .return_format = "structured"
)
second <- run(
  agent,
  question = "Which river runs through it?",
  .history = get_history(first),
  .return_format = "structured"
)

RLM

dsprrr mirrors DSPy’s RLM model—an interpreter per invocation, graph-visible generate_action and extract predictors, llm_query() / llm_query_batched() (including text + image slices), selectable reasoning_mode, multi-turn .history, and repairable typed SUBMIT() validation—while executing R code with signature inputs staged under .context. See How RLM works for the complete contract and limits, and Investigate a regression with RLM for a worked example.

Boundary DSPy dsprrr
Generated language Python R, with inputs under .context
Interpreter binding Per-call interpreter_factory or global setting Bound on rlm_module(), or managed mcp-repl sandbox by default in rlm()
Local persistent runner LocalInterpreter (CPython) r_code_runner(persistent = TRUE) (trusted callr process)
Typed outputs Pydantic / signature adapters ellmer string, number, integer, boolean, enum, array, and object types
Host tools Interpreter-defined Execute in the host R process outside the runner

Assertions

DSPy 3.0 removed dspy.Assert/dspy.Suggest in favor of BestOfN/Refine. dsprrr keeps both: declarative output assertions with retry feedback (with_assertions(), assert_output(), suggest_output()) and the best_of_n() / refine() wrappers.

Optimizers (teleprompters)

DSPy dsprrr Fidelity notes
LabeledFewShot LabeledFewShot Equivalent for root prediction modules; rejects nested graphs
BootstrapFewShot BootstrapFewShot Compiles pipelines jointly; rejects programs containing flex() or rlm_module()
BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch Random search over labeled/bootstrapped candidates; rejects flex() / rlm_module()
MIPROv2 MIPROv2 Searches demos + instructions via a UCB1 bandit (rather than Bayesian optimization); nested graphs require max_bootstrapped_demos = 0L
SIMBA SIMBA Simplified adaptation: hard-example mining + LLM-generated rules
GEPA GEPA Reflective evolution for instructions and flex() sources, with feedback metrics, multi-objective Pareto selection, separate .reflection_llm, and checkpoint resume on plain predictor graphs
COPRO COPRO Equivalent (coordinate ascent over model-rewritten instructions)
KNNFewShot KNNFewShot Equivalent
ReAnchor (experimental) ReAnchor() (experimental) Same gap-midpoint search and fold check; single prediction modules only
Ensemble ensemble() Direct module constructor rather than a teleprompter
BetterTogether BetterTogether Chains prompt optimizers via strategy strings (no weight finetuning)
BootstrapFinetune, GRPO Not available Planned; dsprrr optimizes prompts and decisions, not model weights
No equivalent GridSearchTeleprompter, optimize_grid() Explicit tidymodels-style parameter and variant sweeps
No equivalent Omni() (experimental) Best-of parallel/sequential exploration plus a continuation optimizer
No equivalent AutoResearch(), MetaHarness() (experimental) Agentic optimization loops over validated module snapshots with sandboxed R analysis

GEPA feedback, reflection models, and checkpoints

Wrap metrics in metric_with_feedback() so failed rows feed diagnostic text into GEPA’s reflection prompt, or metric_with_trace() to score execution traces as well. Pass .reflection_llm to separate proposal generation from task evaluation (.llm), and set checkpoint_path / resume = TRUE in optimizer_control() to pause and resume sequential round_robin searches over plain prediction modules and built-in pipelines (see ?GEPA for exact checkpoint rules):

feedback_metric <- metric_with_feedback(
  function(prediction, expected) {
    if (identical(prediction$answer, expected$answer)) {
      list(score = 1, feedback = "Correct.")
    } else {
      list(
        score = 0,
        feedback = paste("Expected", expected$answer, "- check the arithmetic.")
      )
    }
  },
  field = "answer"
)

compiled <- compile(
  qa,
  GEPA(metric = feedback_metric, generations = 5L),
  trainset,
  valset = devset,
  .llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-luna"),
  .reflection_llm = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-astra"),
  control = optimizer_control(
    checkpoint_path = "gepa-search.rds",
    max_metric_calls = 50L
  )
)

Decision types and ReAnchor()

Like DSPy 3.4, dsprrr keeps the output space in the signature and attaches tunable thresholds, cuts, or weights to the module with with_decisions():

sig <- signature(
  inputs = list(input("pair", description = "Two listings")),
  output_type = ellmer::type_object(
    match = ellmer::type_boolean("Are they the same item?")
  )
)
matcher <- module(sig) |> with_decisions(match = decision_bool(threshold = 0.7))
tuned <- compile(
  matcher,
  ReAnchor(metric = metric_exact_match(field = "match")),
  pair_train,
  valset = pair_val
)
decision_settings(tuned)

See Calibrated decisions for decision_score(), decision_choice(), and decision_evidence().

Signatures, composition, and infrastructure

Area DSPy dsprrr
Signatures String notation or dspy.Signature class; with_instructions() signature("a -> b: int") or input() + ellmer types; immutable with_instructions() / append_instructions()
Multimodal inputs dspy.Image, dspy.Audio, dspy.File ellmer Content objects (images, PDFs)
Composition Python dspy.Module subclass with forward() pipeline() / %>>% + step() (jointly compilable), or module_fn() for custom R control flow
LM client & adapters dspy.LM (lm15), XML/Chat/JSON adapters Provider-neutral ellmer Chat + chat_structured() (no separate adapter layer)
Configuration & caching dspy.configure(), dspy.context(), two-tier cache dsp_configure(), with_lm(), local_lm(), two-tier configure_cache()
Async & streaming acall / aforward, streamify() run_async() (Predict, ReAct, factory code modules), run_stream() + stream_listener(), stream_async()
Saving programs save() / load() Versioned whole-program artifacts (save_program(), load_program(), pin_module_config())
Evaluation & traces dspy.Evaluate, MLflow/OTel callbacks evaluate(), eval_program(), export_traces(), session_cost(), plus vitals integration

What dsprrr has that DSPy doesn’t

Feature What it gives you
tidymodels integration llm_predict() parsnip engine, yardstick scoring, and dials parameters (temperature(), top_p(), reasoning_effort())
vitals integration as_vitals_solver(), as_vitals_task(), and as_dsprrr_metric()
ragnar integration Built-in DuckDB hybrid search via rag_module() and ragnar_tool()
Assertions with backtracking Maintained alongside best_of_n() / refine() after removal in DSPy 3.0
Grid search compilation optimize_grid() and GridSearchTeleprompter() for explicit sweeps
Meta & agentic harnesses (experimental) Omni(), AutoResearch(), and MetaHarness()

Roadmap gaps

Key capabilities not yet implemented in dsprrr:

  1. Custom input staging for interpreter-backed modules beyond r_code_runner(persistent = TRUE) and JSON-serialized mcp-repl inputs.
  2. Concurrent execution and checkpoint resume for executable flex() modules and calibrated decision modules.
  3. Whole-program decision calibration (calibrating ReAnchor() across composed pipelines rather than single prediction modules) and RLM child-demo bootstrapping in MIPROv2().
  4. Package-level OpenTelemetry spans layered on top of ellmer’s provider telemetry, and a dedicated typed reasoning output field analogous to dspy.Reasoning.
  5. Model-weight and RL optimization (BootstrapFinetune, GRPO).

Checked against DSPy 3.5.0 (2026-11-10). If one of these gaps blocks your work, please open an issue.
